The integral of 3e^(2x) from x=0 to x=5 is **3/2 (e^10 − 1) ≈ 33038.2**.

I entered the query on wolframalpha.com and the result page showed this as the definite integral. The page also gives the indefinite antiderivative (3e^(2x))/2 + constant, which matches the answer: (3/2)e^10 − (3/2)e^0 = 3/2(e^10 − 1).
